papers.title: Poles Are Not Enough: Zeros of Dyson-Schwinger Gluon Propagators in Yang-Mills Thermodynamics
papers.abstract: A normalized two-point function with several poles does not, on its own, fix the source-free thermal partition function. For the Gaussian measure of the original gluon field, a positive-residue rational propagator contributes determinants from its poles and from zeros interlaced between them. The zero factors distinguish this completion from a gas of independent pole fields and restore two ultraviolet polarizations per adjoint eigenvalue at every finite truncation. We apply the construction to a background-covariant completion of the elliptic Dyson-Schwinger gluon kernel. The first-order SU(3) transition is already present with a single pole, and the saturated six-pole result shifts $T_c/M_g$ by only $1.48\%$, where $T_c$ is the coexistence temperature and $M_g$ is the lowest pole mass. At six poles, the zero determinants raise $T_c/M_g$ by $2.31\%$ and lower $L/T_c^4$ by $12.4\%$, where $L$ is the latent heat and each prescription uses its own $T_c$. At fixed $M_g$ the dimensional latent heat decreases by $4.0\%$. The fixed-holonomy free-energy difference gives an ultraviolet test independent of the additive pressure normalization. At fixed pole number $P$, its asymptotic value agrees with the two-polarization Weiss result when the zeros are retained and is $(3P-1)/2$ times as large in the poles-only prescription.

papers.title: A Positive Turn: Coupled Quintessence and Cosmological Neutrino Masses
papers.abstract: In $\Lambda$CDM, the CMB and DESI BAO upper limits on the total neutrino mass are in tension with the lower bounds from oscillation experiments, and analyses allowing negative effective masses favor negative values. We investigate whether a coupled quintessence (CQ) model in which dark matter interacts with a canonical scalar field $\phi$ through an exponential mass coupling $m_{\rm c}(\phi)\propto e^{-\beta\phi/M_{\rm Pl}}$ can alleviate this tension. Combining CMB, DESI, and supernova data, we find that CQ yields neutrino-mass constraints comparable to those obtained in CPL and consistent with oscillation experiments within $2\sigma$ for normal ordering, without requiring the scalar-field equation of state to cross the phantom divide. We further show that it alleviates the tension more effectively than alternative interacting dark energy models that instead favor more negative effective masses. This comparison shows that whether dark sector interactions can relax neutrino mass bounds ultimately depends on the interplay of their effects on primary CMB anisotropies, geometry, growth, and lensing.

papers.title: Constraining Dark Matter Gravitational Production with the 21cm Signal at the Cosmic Dawn
papers.abstract: The origin of dark matter is one of the major problems in modern cosmology. We can infer its existence from the gravitational potential wells around astrophysical objects, but there is no convincing explanation for what its nature and origin are. Moreover, experiments for direct detection, indirect detection, or particle production in accelerators have not shown, until now, any conclusive interaction between dark matter and particles in the standard model. This may imply that dark matter does not interact with ordinary matter and originates from pure gravitational interaction. In this manuscript, we investigate the possibility to constrain the gravitational production of dark matter from the 21cm brightness temperature at the cosmic dawn. Considering only the time when the absorption profile occurs, we can impose upper limits on the dark matter's mass. Future measurements have potential to extend current constraints and help understanding the nature of dark matter.

papers.title: Enhanced Early Structure from Axiodilatons & 21cm Observations
papers.abstract: Axiodilatons provide a promising unified model of the Dark Sector whose properties are motivated by the use of accidental approximate symmetries to embed the light fields needed for observations into well-motivated UV physics in a technically natural way. These models turn out to help ameliorate many current puzzles in $\Lambda$CDM phenomenology (e.g. the Hubble tension and the evidence for evolving Dark Energy) `for free' despite not being designed for that purpose. We here explore in more detail another serendipitous feature of these models: their tendency to enhance early structure formation, in a way that seems suggestive given the accumulating evidence for structure arising earlier than expected in $\Lambda$CDM. Since early structure growth is the cleanest to study we explore in detail the expected 21cm signal produced by axiodilaton models, using the same parameter choices that improve agreement with observations elsewhere in cosmology. For fixed astrophysics, we forecast that SKA1-Low could distinguish dilaton couplings as small as a few times $10^{-2}$ from $\Lambda$CDM at $2\sigma$, mainly because of the earlier formation of structure. We provide complete derivations of the mass dependence of the relevant cosmological observables, including how dilaton-dependent baryon and electron masses affect the hyperfine transition, the Ly$\alpha$ coupling, X-ray heating and ionization during cosmic dawn and the epoch of reionization. We provide details of radiative transfer, atomic physics and the equations governing the thermal and ionization state of the intergalactic medium.

papers.title: Cosmological Signals from Finite-Lifetime Domain Wall Networks
papers.abstract: We study cosmological perturbations sourced by metastable domain wall (DW) networks. Using the unconnected segment model, we derive analytic expressions for the scalar and tensor power spectra in the long-wavelength regime, finding a fixed ratio between their amplitudes during the scaling regime. These spectra grow as the network evolves, driven by the increasing correlation length and slower redshifting of the wall energy density relative to radiation, and peak at a scale set by the network's collapse time. Comparing the scalar spectrum with observational constraints, we derive bounds on the DW energy density at collapse, which we apply to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ and axion models. When these bounds are saturated, the resulting CMB $B$-mode signal can be comparable to or larger than the inflationary signal for a tensor-to-scalar ratio $r \sim 0.03$, potentially bringing it within reach of future CMB polarization experiments.

papers.title: The NANOGrav 15-year data set: A Limit on Continuous Spin Gravitons
papers.abstract: Continuous spin particles (CSPs) are massless particles characterized by a dimensionful spin scale, $\rho$, which, when non-zero, changes their helicity under Lorentz boosts. Since CSPs reduce to ordinary particles when $\rho \rightarrow 0$, the photon or graviton could be CSPs and only appear to behave as ordinary particles due to a small value of $\rho$. Therefore, it is important to determine what value of $\rho$ is experimentally allowed. Recent work has shown that the physical effects of CSPs scale as powers of $\rho/\omega$ when $\rho \ll \omega$, where $\omega$ is a frequency scale, making low-frequency probes particularly beneficial for highlighting these phenomena. In this paper we use pulsar timing arrays to set constraints on the spin scale of the continuous spin graviton. Pulsar timing arrays are uniquely suited for this application as they have exceptional sensitivity to low, nanohertz frequency gravitational waves, as demonstrated by their recent evidence for a stochastic gravitational wave background. Using standard Bayesian data analysis techniques, we find that the NANOGrav 15-year data set constrains the graviton spin scale to $\rho_\text{g} < 1.23 \times 10^{-23} \, \text{eV} $ at the 95% credible level.

papers.title: Quantum Computing Enhanced Search for Wavelike Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Identifying a weak, stochastic signal hidden within a broad frequency band is a central challenge in the search for wavelike dark matter. We explore quantum computing enhanced sensing based on the Grover search algorithm to address this problem and find that a long integration time stabilizes the accumulated sensing phase, reducing quantum signal processing (QSP) errors induced by dark matter fluctuations. We further propose alternating the signs of the QSP angles between oracle calls to suppress the coherent accumulation of the intrinsic QSP approximation errors during the search. Combining these strategies in a transmon-based benchmark, we obtain a projected sensitivity to axion dark matter beyond existing astrophysical limits. This opens access to substantial unexplored parameter space across the $10$-$100\,\mu\mathrm{eV}$ mass range and offers an accelerated discovery channel for wavelike dark matter. With $10^6$ entangled sensing qubits, the projected sensitivity reaches the QCD axion band. Although illustrated with transmons, the protocol can be adapted to other experimental platforms for wavelike dark matter detection.

papers.title: Rapidly Spinning Primordial Black Holes from Confinement
papers.abstract: Confinement can turn widely separated particles into rapidly spinning primordial black holes. A flux tube pulls a heavy quark--antiquark pair together, converting its stored energy into relativistic motion. The same mechanism is possible in the magnetic dual, where a Higgs phase confines magnetic flux into a string joining a monopole--antimonopole pair. As the particles approach, cosmological tides and string bends can deflect their motion and make them miss. These disturbances can originate during inflation or be generated later. Black-hole formation then requires rare close passages from a smooth, broad encounter distribution. The resulting natal spin density therefore rises linearly to extremality, with mean dimensionless spin two thirds. Numerical string evolutions recover this law. Pairs that miss can remain bound, radiate and later collapse into lighter, near-extremal holes, sourcing a stochastic gravitational-wave background. Although the abundance remains model dependent, confinement leaves a unique spin signature that gravitational-wave observations can test.

papers.title: Enhancing Graviton--Photon Conversion through Galactic Magnetic Turbulence
papers.abstract: Plasma dispersion suppresses coherent graviton-photon conversion over astrophysical distances. We show that Galactic magnetic turbulence enables phase matching by compensating the plasma-induced mismatch, allowing matched magnetic modes to contribute coherently. In the long path limit, the ensemble-averaged conversion probability grows linearly with propagation distance in the phase matched regime and is governed by the projected magnetic power spectrum. Applied to photon background observations, this mechanism yields characteristic strain limits that are stronger than previous Galactic conversion bounds in the inertial range phase matching window, with improvements of up to two orders of magnitude.

papers.title: Triple-Massive-Exchange Bispectrum of Quasi-Single-Field Inflation
papers.abstract: The triple-exchange bispectrum of the scalar quasi-single-field inflation model has resisted analytic evaluation across its full parameter space since its advent, despite rapid progress in cosmological collider physics. In this Letter, we solve it for general mass and mixing strength as a convergent double series, by applying the Mellin-Barnes representation directly to the mixed propagator between the massless and massive modes. The result is exact, non-perturbative, and physically transparent; the method is broadly applicable.

papers.title: The Dark Side of the Periodic Table: Theory and Signatures of Nuclear Atomic Dark Matter
papers.abstract: We study the theory and signatures of a Mirror Twin Higgs (MTH) scenario in which stable twin neutrons constitute most of the dark matter (DM), while a subdominant component of twin elements survives as nuclear atomic dark matter (naDM). This framework offers a solution to the $matter~coincidence~problem$ ($\Omega_{\rm DM}\simeq5\Omega_b$), as the twin $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry can correlate the visible and DM mass scales and their number densities. We analyze twin nucleon freeze-out and the onset of twin Big Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN) to estimate the total naDM abundance, and determine which elements in the dark periodic table could be populated. An appreciable but subdominant naDM component generally requires a fractional nucleon mass splitting near the percent level, with twin-BBN creating heavy elements up to twin carbon. Strong twin neutron-proton scattering allows nearly all of the dark matter, not only the atomic sub-component, to participate in $dark~acoustic~oscillations$ (DAO) at early times, giving rise to a characteristic two-stage DAO signature that may be detected with future cosmological probes. Interactions between the twin and visible sectors, including the irreducible Higgs portal, make this scenario a well-motivated target for future directional direct-detection searches, and the naDM sub-component is expected to exhibit highly exotic astrophysics. We outline a supersymmetric twin Froggatt-Nielsen realization in which spontaneous $\mathbb{Z}_2$ breaking in the flavon sector can generate the required fermion spectrum and Higgs potential.

papers.title: Dual-species atom interferometry for axion dark matter
papers.abstract: Atom interferometers are sensitive to oscillations of the masses and transition frequencies of atoms, which can be induced by axion dark matter. The main limitation is the sensitivity to gravity gradient noise (GGN). We propose a dual-species atom interferometry sequence that provides a suppression of GGN by up to three orders of magnitude and a sensitivity enhancement via the mass difference of the two atoms. We show that, under realistic experimental assumptions, a 10m-baseline dual-species atom interferometer is more sensitive to the axion gluon coupling than a 100m single-species gradiometer. Including a comprehensive noise analysis, we demonstrate that the Very Long Baseline Atom Interferometer (VLBAI) in Hannover with a baseline of 10m can probe the axion decay constant at levels almost competitive with leading laboratory constraints. The proposed 100m-baseline Atom Interferometer CERN Experiment (AICE) can extend this sensitivity by up to two orders of magnitude, surpassing laboratory constraints for axion masses of $10^{-19}\;\text{eV}/c^2 \lesssim m_a \lesssim 3\times10^{-15}\;\text{eV}/c^2$.

papers.title: The Curious Case of Anapole Dark Matter at LZ: Minimal, Elastic and Testable
papers.abstract: Majorana fermions can carry neither charge nor dipole moments, leaving the anapole moment as their leading electromagnetic interaction. A stable Majorana fermion is therefore a minimal realization of electromagnetically interacting dark matter. The momentum dependence of the anapole interaction produces a harder recoil spectrum than standard momentum-independent interactions. We show that this makes elastically scattering anapole dark matter a viable interpretation of the single high-energy nuclear-recoil event recorded by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment, in a region where almost no background is expected. Curiously, the same coupling that fits the LZ data also yields the observed dark matter abundance at a mass of about 300 GeV, and is consistent with collider searches and indirect detection. The scenario is testable, predicting further events at lower energies, which the full LZ run will probe and a next-generation detector such as XLZD will decisively test.

papers.title: Silent Heavy Fields: An Exclusion Rule for the Cosmological Collider
papers.abstract: The cosmological collider uses oscillatory signatures in primordial correlators to probe heavy fields during inflation. This probe has blind spots, as heavy fields can keep ticking in time while remaining silent in the correlators. In this letter, we derive an exclusion rule under which cosmological collider signals vanish. The rule covers two classes of diagrams where a de Sitter invariant heavy sector couples covariantly to a single external field at one vertex. We first prove it for exchanges mediated by the two-point function of the heavy sector to all loop orders, using a spectral decomposition followed by a field redefinition. The result then extends to one-loop polygons by matching their oscillatory contributions onto those of the first class. The approximate signals of previously studied processes that fall into these classes must therefore be revisited. As a nonvanishing example, we derive the leading signal of a triangle loop for the first time in a toy model motivated by chemical potentials.

papers.title: Mapping Domain-Wall Bayesian Reconstruction with LISA
papers.abstract: We study the Bayesian reconstruction of peaked domain-wall gravitational-wave signals with LISA and construct reconstruction maps over the signal-parameter plane. These maps identify regions where the signal can be probed with minimal posterior uncertainty and parameter degeneracy. Our analysis employs a two-parameter domain-wall spectral template and includes astrophysical foregrounds from Galactic double-white-dwarf binaries and extragalactic compact binaries, together with LISA instrumental noise. Bayesian inference is performed for 64 injections using nested sampling, and the resulting posterior quantities are interpolated with the Clough--Tocher method to generate smooth maps across parameter space. Under the adopted instrumental-noise and foreground assumptions, we find that LISA reconstructs domain-wall signals most effectively for annihilation temperatures $T_*\sim10^3\!-\!10^6\,\mathrm{GeV}$. In this regime, posteriors become tighter and less degenerate, enabling reliable two-parameter reconstruction. The most favorable region corresponds to signals with ${\rm SNR}\gtrsim50$, while signals with ${\rm SNR}\sim10$ remain reconstructable near $T_*\sim10^{5-6}\,\mathrm{GeV}$. This weaker-signal region corresponds approximately to $4\times10^{-12}\lesssim\Omega_{\rm GW}^{\rm peak}h^2\lesssim4\times10^{-11}$ and $30\,\mathrm{mHz}\lesssim f_p\lesssim100\,\mathrm{mHz}$. Our results provide a quantitative reconstruction forecast for peaked domain-wall signals in the LISA band and a guide for particle-physics models predicting milli-Hz gravitational-wave spectra.

papers.title: Ultraviolet Structure of the Gravitational-Wave Response in a Time-Dependent Scalar Medium
papers.abstract: We study the real-time linear response of gravitational waves in an FLRW background with a scalar field of general time-dependent effective mass. In the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, we develop an adiabatic regularization scheme for unequal-time correlation functions and use it to extract the ultraviolet structure of the one-loop response. The leading divergence reproduces the familiar $\Box ^2h_{ij}$ structure, whereas the time-dependent background induces additional local divergences proportional to $\Box h_{ij}$, $\partial_\tau h_{ij}$, and $h_{ij}$. These are renormalized by local counterterms associated with the Weyl-squared term, a time-dependent Ricci-scalar term, a time-dependent cosmological constant, and the Ricci-scalar-squared term $R^2$. The same counterterms also remove the ultraviolet divergences of the background tadpole stress tensor and agree with the known covariant counterterm results. In a flat-background Mathieu oscillator example, replacing the adiabatic vacuum by the instantaneous vacuum leaves these counterterms unchanged but introduces an initial-surface divergence, which is absorbed into the initial data rather than the bulk counterterms.

papers.title: Dynamical flattening of halo density cusps by Q-ball dark matter
papers.abstract: Cold, collisionless dark matter successfully explains a wide range of observations, including the formation of large-scale structure. Nevertheless, tensions remain on small, galactic scales, most notably the cusp-core, or inner-mass-deficit, problem and the diversity of inner rotation-curve shapes and central densities at fixed halo mass. These observations suggest that additional dark-sector physics may affect the inner structure of halos, although no generally accepted explanation has yet emerged. Here, making use of a toy but representative model, we investigate how interacting dark-matter Q-balls -- non-topological solitons stabilized by a conserved charge -- modify halo centers and generate a diversity of inner profiles. Our calculations include merger-induced mass and kinetic-energy losses, elastic heat transport, and the gravitational readjustment of the halo; flattening and later recontraction can both occur. Produced in the early Universe in the dark sector, these Q-balls grow in the dense central regions of halos, while their interaction cross section decreases as the soliton mass increases. This process operates preferentially in halo centers, converting part of the rest-mass energy stored in massive Q-balls into relativistic dark-sector particles and thereby modifying the inner mass-density profile. The resulting density-dependent energy loss competes with heat transport and halo response. An ensemble of initial assembly conditions yields very different final densities at fixed microphysics, although neither a universal constant-density core nor a statistical fit to the observed population is established.

papers.title: Heavy neutral leptons beyond the BBN bound: probing the lepton asymmetry of the Universe
papers.abstract: Hadronically decaying particles with lifetimes $\tau\gtrsim0.02\,{\rm s}$ are excluded by Big Bang Nucleosynthesis almost independently of their abundance: the mesons from their decays convert protons into neutrons faster than the reverse, and helium is overproduced. For heavy neutral leptons (HNLs), this blankets the couplings the upcoming accelerator searches can reach. We propose a scenario with large lepton flavor asymmetries in which HNLs evade it. A Dirac HNL decays into $\pi^+$ and its antiparticle into $\pi^-$, so an asymmetry between the two populations injects an excess of $\pi^+$, which converts the neutrons back to their standard abundance, while a cancellation between the asymmetries and the HNL decays keeps the shift in $N_{\rm eff}$ small. This opens the parameter space with $m_l+m_\pi\lesssim m_N\lesssim1\,{\rm GeV}$ and $\tau_N\lesssim1\,{\rm s}$, including a substantial region within the reach of SHiP. A discovery there, combined with the BBN and CMB observables, would fix the primordial flavor asymmetries up to one remaining direction. The relic neutrino background and gravitational waves from the QCD transition epoch may probe that direction, and with it the lepton asymmetry of the Universe.

papers.title: Forward BFKL evolution at fixed coupling as a random walk, and the loss of its probability law at fixed next-to-leading order
papers.abstract: The BFKL equation describes how the density of gluons in a hadron grows with the collision energy. This evolution is often treated as a random walk in the logarithm of the gluon transverse momentum, but it has not been established that one set of positive step probabilities describes this walk in the size and the direction of the momentum, or that such probabilities exist beyond leading order. We show that one positive step density describes the evolution in the size and the direction of the momentum with no approximation at leading order, fixed coupling and zero momentum transfer, once the gluon density is rescaled by the size of its transverse momentum and its growth is divided out. The displacements of the resulting walk over separate, equal intervals of rapidity, the logarithm of the energy in units of a reference energy, are then independent and identically distributed, which makes the walk a Levy process. We also show that this description fails when the series in the coupling is cut at next-to-leading order, with the reference energy and the scale of the coupling both set by the product of the transverse momenta before and after an emission. The evolution averaged over directions then has no probability law at any fixed positive coupling and rapidity, because a negative correction growing as the squared logarithm of the momentum ratio outweighs the leading term when one momentum is much larger than the other. A positive step density for the averaged walk agrees with this truncated evolution to next-to-leading order and defines a random walk for every value of the strong coupling below one, so the failure comes from the truncation. The main message is that agreement with perturbation theory does not guarantee positive step probabilities, so an evolution equation summed to all orders and meant to describe a random walk must be tested for them.

papers.title: Active learning at a graduate summer school: feasibility, student response, and the role of instructor training
papers.abstract: Active learning is becoming standard practice in undergraduate STEM instruction in North America and is slowly being adopted in graduate courses. Graduate summer schools, one- to two-week programs in which students from many institutions gather for intensive, specialized instruction in their field, are common in physics; they are taught by researchers chosen for their expertise, and their pedagogy remains almost entirely traditional lecturing. We report a study at a one-week graduate school in neutrino and astroparticle physics attended by 38 students from 8 countries. Six lecturers with limited or no prior experience of teaching with active learning introduced Peer Instruction-style active learning into their lectures after approximately four hours of preparation led by a physics-education specialist. Each of the three main lecture streams was taught traditionally on one day and in the active format on the other. Students were surveyed after each of the first two days and at the end of the week; all six instructors were surveyed as well. In every active lecture, spanning three instructors and three topics, 82-100% of respondents reported that the interactive segments helped them stay engaged and check their understanding, and in every stream the difficulty was rated as better matched on the active day. At the end of the week, 33 of 36 wanted such teaching in future graduate courses, and not one respondent disagreed. All six instructors judged the approach productive and intend to use it again; only two found implementation straightforward. With brief expert-led preparation, lecturers new to active learning implemented it successfully for a heterogeneous audience, and both students and instructors want more. The school was also the first time any of the six instructors implemented structured active learning: a summer school can develop its lecturers as well as its students.

papers.title: Impact of dynamical, quadratic, and higher-order tidal effects on gravitational-wave observations of binary neutron stars
papers.abstract: Neutron-star binaries are prime gravitational-wave sources for current and next-generation detectors, and provide a unique probe for the behaviour of nuclear matter at supranuclear densities. Extracting information about this requires accurate waveform models that capture tidal effects during the late inspiral. We incorporate state-of-the-art tidal corrections into a post-Newtonian inspiral waveform, including dynamical tides and nonlinear contributions from quadratic Love numbers through eighth post-Newtonian (8PN) order. Using Bayesian model comparison, we find that these corrections can significantly affect the gravitational-wave signal, with the 8PN tidal response becoming comparable to lower-PN tidal contributions in the subsolar-mass regime. For exceptionally loud GW170817-like binaries observed by third-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope, higher-order tidal effects can be distinguished with high statistical significance, while neglecting them can introduce substantial biases in the inferred tidal deformabilities and, consequently, in constraints on the neutron-star equation of state. These corrections are particularly relevant for putative subsolar-mass binaries: the lower compactness of their constituents enhances tidal effects and makes them potentially important even for current detectors. Our results highlight the importance of higher-order tidal corrections for precision gravitational-wave measurements of dense nuclear matter.

papers.title: Bayesian Inference of Fermionic Dark Matter Admixed Neutron Stars Informed by Galaxy Cluster Constraints
papers.abstract: Self-interacting dark matter is constrained on galactic and cluster scales by its elastic scattering cross section per unit mass, $\sigma/m_\chi \sim 0.1-10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. We incorporate this cross section into the equation of state of an asymmetric, self-interacting fermionic dark matter component and perform a Bayesian inference of dark matter admixed neutron stars in the two-fluid framework at $\sigma/m_\chi = 0.1$, $1$ and $10\ {\rm cm^2/g}$. Seven nuclear matter parameters are sampled together with the dark particle mass and mass fraction, and confronted with nuclear theory and neutron star observations. The nuclear sector and the global observables are statistically indistinguishable across the whole range of cross sections, while the data constrain the dark matter mass to $m_\chi \simeq 1.45-1.88$~GeV and its mass fraction to $f_\chi \simeq 0.05-0.09$, depending on the cross section. Finally, comparing runs built from the same parameter draws, so that only the cross section differs, we find that it does change the baryonic radius appreciably, but only for light dark matter, a region the astrophysical data largely disfavor. The self-interaction is therefore not too weak to be seen; however its effect is hidden in the region of parameter space that the present observational data already disfavor.

papers.title: Probing Ultralight Higher-spin Dark Matter using Stellar Kinematics of Dwarf Galaxies
papers.abstract: Stellar kinematics of the classical Milky Way dwarf galaxies provide a powerful probe of the dark matter distribution and its underlying physics. In this article we use them to explore ultralight dark matter (ULDM) with a non-zero spin. Numerical simulations in the non-relativistic limit have shown that, for the same initial conditions, higher-spin ULDM forms a more diffuse soliton core at the galactic center, with a smoother transition to the NFW outer region, than scalar ULDM. We introduce a generalized parametrization of the ULDM halo profile that captures these spin-induced effects through three additional parameters: the normalization of the central core density, the exponent of the core-halo mass relation, and the radius of the transition to the NFW envelope. Applying this profile in a Bayesian analysis of six classical dwarf galaxies, we find halo masses in the range $10^{8.5}$-$10^{9.5}\,M_\odot$ and, from each galaxy individually, a particle mass $m \gtrsim 3\times10^{-21}$ eV. The core-halo exponent and the transition radius are consistent with their scalar values. The core-density normalization is also consistent with the scalar value in four galaxies and prefers a core denser than a scalar soliton in Fornax, while the factor-of-several suppression expected for higher-spin cores is not excluded by any single galaxy. The data therefore show no preference for the more diffuse cores of higher-spin ULDM, but do not yet rule them out.

papers.title: SuSy and CoDy Radiation from Evaporating Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay between physics beyond the Standard Model and modified spacetime geometries in shaping the photon and neutrino spectra from evaporating black holes. We implement three representative supersymmetric (SuSy) benchmarks and a composite dynamics (CoDy) scenario in BlackHawk. We consider both Schwarzschild black holes and regular black holes geometries, namely polymerized, Hayward, and Simpson--Visser black holes. New degrees of freedom at the TeV scale become accessible at Hawking temperatures corresponding to black hole masses of approximately $M_{\rm BH}\sim 10^{10}\,\mathrm{g}$. We show that physics beyond the Standard Model produces distinctive signatures in both the instantaneous secondary-photon and neutrino spectra. Radiative decays generate narrow spectral features with approximately temperature-independent relative amplitudes, while multistep decay cascades produce broad enhancements that become increasingly pronounced at higher temperatures. In contrast, compressed mass spectra exhibit no localized features. Crucially, we show that the effects of new particle physics and modified spacetime geometries can become intertwined in specific energy regimes, altering the resulting spectral signatures. Our results demonstrate that photon and neutrino spectra provide complementary probes of new particle physics and black hole geometry, with predicted spectral enhancements extending into the energy ranges accessible to current and future high-energy observatories.

papers.title: New Physics in Ultra-High-Energy Neutrino Flavor
papers.abstract: Neutrino flavor measurements test physics beyond the Standard Model that modifies neutrino production, propagation, or detection. IceCube has measured the flavor composition of the astrophysical neutrino flux up to PeV energies. Next-generation experiments will extend flavor measurements to the ultra-high-energy (UHE) regime, $100\,\mathrm{PeV}$-$10\,\mathrm{EeV}$, by combining in-ice radio detection with Earth-skimming tau neutrinos. We present the first study of the new-physics reach of these projected UHE flavor measurements. We take Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) as a benchmark, since its effects grow as a power of the neutrino energy. We find that UHE flavor ratios will be the most sensitive probe of LIV for operators of dimension four and higher, improving on current bounds from all sectors by up to twenty orders of magnitude. Three-flavor observables improve this sensitivity by up to an order of magnitude over Earth-skimming tau neutrinos alone.

papers.title: A unified mean-field description of dense hadron matter constrained from $\chi$EFT and lattice QCD
authors: Md. Emanuel Hoque (Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics/HBNI)
Arunava Mukherjee (Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics/HBNI)
Sayantan Sharma (The Institute of Mathematical Sciences/HBNI)
papers.abstract: We construct a relativistic mean field theory (RMFT) of hadrons in an attempt to describe the confined phase of QCD across a wide range of temperatures and baryon densities. This includes the scalar and vector mesons interacting with baryons and resonances up to $3$ GeV, including those which are not yet discovered but predicted within the quark model and lattice QCD. The baryon--meson couplings are constrained through a two-stage Bayesian analysis. In the first stage, we constrain six different couplings in our theory using six nuclear empirical parameters inferred from the chiral effective field theory predictions of the energy per nucleon for pure neutron matter over baryon densities $n_B \in [0.08, 0.32]~\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$, employing a Gaussian-process likelihood to account for correlations in the input data. In the second stage, this posterior is set as the prior for constraining different baryon--meson couplings in our RMFT construction, using lattice QCD input. The resulting posterior provides substantially improved constraints for different baryon--meson couplings and non-linear meson self-interactions, which are consistent with the current astrophysical observations of neutron star masses, radii and tidal deformability parameters.

papers.title: Toward the minimal set of states in axion superradiance
papers.abstract: Observational searches for black hole superradiance require predicting the growth and evolution of quasi-bound states on astrophysical timescales. For axions (and most light spin-0 particles), self-interactions efficiently redistribute energy and angular momentum from the fastest-growing superradiant states into higher-order, more weakly bound states, and do so on short timescales. This has made it difficult to compute even the most mundane of observables across large regions of parameter space. In this work we extend the study of self-interacting systems, following the evolution of nearly 300 coupled quasi-bound states. We evolve a $10\,M_\odot$ black hole over a Salpeter timescale, and $10^4$ and $10^8\,M_\odot$ black holes over a Gyr, identifying for each axion mass the minimal set of states required to describe the evolution of the black hole and the shape of the superradiant cloud. In most cases the evolution converges as increasingly weakly bound states are added; we identify no less than 203 distinct quasi-bound states that play a role in establishing this convergence. In small regions of parameter space, however, we find no converged solution, and show that broad resonant features and nearly degenerate scattering rates redistribute mass to bound states with principal quantum numbers $n \gtrsim 45$. We further show that the cloud can extend to radii orders of magnitude larger than usually assumed, that gravitational-wave level transitions can prevent the growth of superradiant states, and that both the gravitational-wave spectrum and the interaction with the environment are far richer than previously appreciated.

papers.title: Dark Matter Velocimetry with Quantum Networks
papers.abstract: Quantum sensor networks can use the spatial phase coherence of wavelike dark matter to probe not only particle properties but also the motion and structure of the Galactic halo. We explore this idea for the minimal two-node network, in which a nonlocal exchange measurement samples the characteristic function of the velocity distribution. We compare the Standard Halo Model (SHM) with a Gaia-inspired radially anisotropic component and their mixture (SHM++), taking into account daily and annual modulation, postselection, depolarizing events, and a flat instrumental offset. We show that annual modulation at one fixed local sidereal time has the same phase waveform for the centered SHM and Gaia-inspired SHM++ models, leaving them degenerate when the overall signal amplitude is unknown. Earth's rotation breaks this degeneracy by scanning the baseline through Galactic directions and exposing the direction-dependent coherence of an anisotropic population. Distinguishing these velocity distributions would test whether the local halo is smooth and nearly isotropic or contains a radially biased accreted component, turning a quantum-network detection into a probe of Milky Way structure. Our likelihood analysis shows how modulation and signal-odd controls separate this information from flat backgrounds and provides a path from model discrimination toward measurement of the local velocity distribution.

papers.title: Dark matter evolution in stellar objects: A Boltzmann transport approach
papers.abstract: Dark matter (DM) captured by stars offers a way to search for physics beyond the Standard Model. We study the evolution of captured DM with the Boltzmann transport equation (BTE), which follows both the abundance and the phase-space distribution of the bound particles from capture toward a stationary state. Averaging over orbital motion, we write the BTE as a master equation in energy and angular momentum that includes capture, scattering between bound orbits, annihilation and evaporation. Applying it to the Sun, we find that captured DM does not thermalize within the solar age when its scattering on nuclei is rare. The bound DM then remains much more extended than the isothermal distribution assumed in the classical treatment, and its annihilation rate can be suppressed by many orders of magnitude. We also apply the BTE to the inelastic Higgsino interpretation of the recent LUX-ZEPLIN result, which involves two DM components coupled through inelastic scattering. The thermal motion of solar nuclei opens capture channels that are closed for nuclei at rest and strengthens the constraint on the mass splitting by tens of keV.

papers.title: Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth's Mantle with Multi-Site Geo-neutrino Measurements
papers.abstract: We present a global fit to geo-neutrino measurements at four underground sites (Kamioka, Gran Sasso, Sudbury, Jiangmen), combining signal rates with site-specific predictions of the lithospheric contribution to constrain the quantity and distribution of radioactivity in the Earth's mantle. Assuming a uniform distribution of radioactivity in the mantle, we find a geo-neutrino rate of $S_\text{mantle} = 14.8 \pm 4.5$ NIU when the lithospheric predictions are allowed to vary within their uncertainties. This uniform mantle signal rate corresponds to radiogenic heating of $18.5 \pm 5.6$ TW. Although the uniform-mantle signal is resolved at $\sim3.2\sigma$, there is noticeable tension between the inferred mantle signals at Jiangmen and Kamioka, which may indicate non-uniform geo-neutrino production in the mantle. We explore six families of models to describe the heterogeneous spatial distribution of radiogenic elements in the Earth's mantle. Each model contains anomalous bodies or reservoirs carrying an excess of heat-producing elements over a depleted mantle (DM) background, with total inventory set by bulk-silicate-Earth mass balance and by a geochemical Th/U constraint. For each model, we compute the geo-response at each detector site and fit the resulting signals to the four measurements. A total of 968,274 individual model configurations are defined and tested. The results of $\sim$3 million distinct fits show that no plausible mantle or lithosphere model applied uniformly to all four sites reproduces the difference between the inferred mantle signals at the Jiangmen and Kamioka sites. Only local, site-specific prescriptions are able to reach the observed difference, suggesting that the Kamioka-Jiangmen tension is due to a local effect or statistical scatter, rather than large-scale mantle structure.
